newsitem.title: UK: Symonds warns of lower-than-expected profit.
newsitem.headline: Symonds warns of lower-than-expected profit.

text.p: British engineering group Symonds Engineering Plc said on Thursday its pretax profits for the year to March 31 would be about 1.5 million stg lower than market expectations.
The company cited previously-disclosed accounting problems at its Precision Engineering division.
Symonds said it would recommend a final dividend of 1.2p to make 1.8p net per share for the year.
The company said it expected Precision to post a loss of more than 1.1 million stg due to mis-statements in management accounts and lower-than-expected sales.
Symonds' shares dropped 5.0p to 30.5 by 0745 GMT.

According to a report by Arthur Andersen, the division's local management had consistently recorded sales where no goods had been despatched in an attempt to cover shortfalls against sales forecasts, Symonds said.
The company said no evidence had been found that any of the management had personally benefitted from any of the actions taken.
Symonds, which disclosed the division's problems in April, said certain staff had been suspended pending possible disciplinary action.
The company had previously sacked the division's managing director, Ken Garner, and replaced him with Patrick Curran.
Arthur Andersen was appointed to investigate the matter independent of Symonds' auditors.
In other news, the company said chief executive Jim Symonds, who had previously planned to retire in June, would leave the group by the end of next month.
Non-executive chairman Rod Ackrill will assume the additional role of chief executive on a temporary basis.
Symonds planned to report results on June 19. --London Newsroom +44 171 542 7717
